==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*deh₃-}}
{{ety|en|:bf|editor|:influence|fr:-|tree=+}}
{{back-form|en|editor}}, influenced by {{uder|en|fr|éditer||edit, publish}} and {{uder|en|la|editus}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|ĕdʹĭt|a=UK}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɛdɪt/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-edit.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{enPR|ĕdʹĭt|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɛdɪt/|[ˈɛɾɪʔ]|[ˈɛɾɪt̚]}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛdɪt|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L12586}}
{{en-noun}}

# A change to the text of a [[document]].
# {{lb|en|computing}} A change in the text of a [[file]], a [[website]] or the code of [[software]].
#: {{ux|en|He has made 5780 '''edits''' on [[Wikipedia]] so far.}}
# An edited piece of [[media]], especially [[video]] [[footage]].
#: {{ux|en|An early '''edit''' of the film included a romantic subplot.}}
# {{lb|en|Internet|specifically}} A [[compilation#Noun|compilation]] of memorable moments (in a [[show#Noun|show]], [[sport#Noun|sport]], etc.), often featuring stylized camera effects and intense [[music#Noun|music]].
#: {{ux|en|a basketball '''edit''', a Thor '''edit'''}}
#: {{ux|en|bro thinks he's in an '''edit''' (Internet meme)}}
# {{lb|en|comedy}} An interruption or change to an [[improvised]] scene.
# {{lb|en|genetics}} An alteration to the [[DNA sequence]] of a [[chromosome]]; an act of [[gene splicing]].
# {{lb|en|fashion}} A [[range]] of [[product]]s related by [[theme]] or [[purpose]].
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=17 June 2015|author=Alison S. Cohn|title=Shopping Events and Sales This Week in New York|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/18/fashion/shopping-events-and-sales-this-week-in-new-york.html|text=The Outnet will release a high-summer '''edit''' of 17 exclusive, limited-edition items including a Eugenia Kim fedora ($175.)|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722163225/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/18/fashion/shopping-events-and-sales-this-week-in-new-york.html|archivedate=22 July 2025}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=7 July 2023|author=Faith Richardson|title=Ashley James’ new Tu '''edit''' has style buys from £6 to support postpartum bodies|titleurl=https://www.ok.co.uk/lifestyle/fashion/ashley-james-tu-summer-clothes-30414844|journal=w:OK!|text=Thankfully, fellow new mum Ashley James has released the ultimate summer '''edit''' with clothing brand Tu that’s not only affordable, but was chosen with postpartum bodies in mind {{...}}|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260924094032/https://www.ok.co.uk/lifestyle/fashion/ashley-james-tu-summer-clothes-30414844|archivedate=24 September 2026}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L175}}
{{en-verb}}

# To [[change]] a [[text]], or a [[document]].
#: {{ux|en|Your speech is too long. You need to '''edit''' it.}}
# To [[alter]] a [[photograph]] or [[recording]] of [[sound]] or [[video]].
#: {{ux|en|We shot an hour-long interview then '''edited''' it down to 45 minutes.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be the [[editor]] of a publication.
#: {{ux|en|He '''edits''' the Chronicle.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1912|author=w:L. Frank Baum|title=Aunt Jane's Nieces on Vacation|chapter=3
|passage="How?" responded Patsy; "why, it's easy enough, Uncle. We'll buy a press, hire a printer, and Beth and Louise will help me '''edit''' the paper. I'm sure I can exhibit literary talents of a high order, once they are encouraged to sprout. Louise writes lovely poetry and 'stories of human interest,' and Beth—"}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} To change the contents of a [[file]], [[website]], etc.
#: {{ux|en|Wikipedia is an interactive encyclopedia which allows anybody to '''edit''' and improve articles.}}
# {{lb|en|biology}} To [[alter]] the [[DNA]] sequence of a [[chromosome]]; to perform [[gene splicing]].
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=26 April 2015|author=Beth Shapiro|title=Could we 'de-extinctify' the woolly mammoth|url=http://www.theguardian.com/science/2015/apr/26/woolly-mammoth-normal-for-norfolk-de-extinction
|passage=Today, the technology to edit '''genomes''' is limited in the number of changes that can be made at once, which is probably one reason why the Harvard team focused on only 14 genes.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261026204029/https://www.theguardian.com/science/2015/apr/26/woolly-mammoth-normal-for-norfolk-de-extinction|archivedate=26 October 2026}}
# To [[assemble]] a [[film]] by [[cut]]ting and [[splice|splicing]] raw [[footage]].
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=December 17 2014|author=Mekado Murphy|title=Below the Line: Editing ‘Boyhood’|url=http://carpetbagger.blogs.nytimes.com/2014/12/17/below-the-line-editing-boyhood/
|passage=When the director approached Ms. Adair about his idea for “Boyhood,” shooting footage each of those 12 years, she immediately agreed to take part. The decision was made to '''edit''' the film progressively, cutting the scenes from each year after they were completed.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220621202437/https://carpetbagger.blogs.nytimes.com/2014/12/17/below-the-line-editing-boyhood/|archivedate=21 June 2022}}
# {{lb|en|comedy}} To cut short or otherwise alter an [[improvised]] scene.
# {{lb|en|ergative}} To lend itself to editing in a certain way.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2018|author=Gary Hudson; Sarah Rowlands|title=The Broadcast Journalism Handbook
|passage=The junior can offer to do the voxes, gaining experience and sparing the senior journalist the trouble. Always remember to think how the clips will '''edit''' together.}}
